name: io.github.Nutshell2000/agent-data-tools-web
title: Agent Data Tools: Web, documents and search
description: 30 tools: web pages, JS apps and PDFs as text, feeds, sitemaps, search. 10 free calls.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Exa-style web search: top 1-20 results with title, URL, snippet, published date and favicon (Brave index); optional domain, date, category and phrase filters; optional live page text, highlights and AI summaries of the top 10 pages. Results are for immediate use only: no storing, resale or model training (Brave API terms). Failures return 503, uncharged. Use when an agent needs current information or sources from the open web. Example: q=x402 payment protocol. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits); failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

includeDomains.description: Only results from these domains: comma list or JSON array, up to 20 (example.com, github.com/org)

excludeDomains.description: Never results from these domains: comma list or JSON array

startPublishedDate.description: Only pages published on or after this date (ISO 8601, e.g. 2025-01-01)

endPublishedDate.description: Only pages published on or before this date (ISO 8601)

category.description: news, research paper, github, pdf, tweet, linkedin profile, company, personal site or financial report

includeText.description: A phrase the results must contain (up to 5 words)

excludeText.description: A phrase the results must not contain

country.description: Localize results for this country: 2-letter code (SE, DE, FR, GB, US…)

textChars.description: Return the live page text of the top results, this many characters each (500-20000, or true for 3000; default none)

highlights.description: true: the passages of each page that best match the query, with scores

summary.description: true: a 1-3 sentence AI summary of each of the top pages

summaryQuery.description: What the summaries should focus on (default: the query)

tools.name: pack_web_research
tools.description: One call to research a question on the web: a Brave web search, then the text of the top 1-5 result pages, read in parallel and clipped to your length, with titles and URLs. A page that cannot be read is listed with its reason. Results are for the caller's immediate use only: no storing, resale or model training (Brave API terms). Use when an agent needs current, sourced information in one step instead of a search plus several page reads. Example: q=x402 payment protocol. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits); failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

q.description: What to research, at most 400 characters

pages.description: How many top results to read in full (1-5, default 3)

maxChars.description: Characters of text per page (500-10000, default 3000)

tools.name: news
tools.description: News headlines on any topic, crypto included, as JSON: title, URL, snippet, publisher domain and age, from the Brave Search API's news index. 1-20 results per call; freshness limits results to the past day, week or month. Results are for the caller's immediate use only: no storing, resale or model training (Brave API terms). Upstream failures return 503, uncharged. Use when an agent needs current news on a topic. Example: q=bitcoin ETF. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits); failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

q.description: News search query, at most 400 characters

freshness.description: Only articles from the past day, week or month (default: any age)

tools.name: pack_news_sentiment
tools.description: Brand sentiment from the news on a topic in one call: the latest headlines from the Brave News index (title, URL, publisher, age), each with a positive or negative score from a DistilBERT model, and the balance across them. Up to 10 articles from the past day, week or month. Not a market signal. Results are for the caller's immediate use only (Brave API terms). Use for a market mood check, brand monitoring or a news brief. Example: q=bitcoin. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits); failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

freshness.description: Only articles from the past day, week or month (default: week)

tools.name: contents
tools.description: Web read: read one to five public web pages in one call and get each one's clean text (or Markdown), title, author and published date where the page declares them, in the request shape search APIs use (urls as a list). Pages are read in parallel; one that cannot be read is listed in statuses with its reason and the rest still answer. Static HTML, Markdown and plain text, up to 20,000 characters a page. Use to read search results in one call. Example: urls=https://example.com,https://www.iana.org/help/example-domains. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

urls.description: One to five page URLs: comma-separated, one per line, or a JSON array

tools.name: image_metadata
tools.description: Read an image's metadata from its URL: format (JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP), width and height, and for JPEG photos the EXIF data: camera make and model, lens, date taken, exposure, aperture, ISO, focal length, orientation, software and the GPS position (latitude, longitude, altitude) when it was recorded. Up to 15 MB. Use to check where and when a photo was taken, verify an upload, or strip-check images before publishing. Example: url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ianare/exif-samples/master/jpg/gps/DSCN0010.jpg. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Public URL of the image

tools.name: url_favicon
tools.description: Find a website's icons: every <link rel=icon>, shortcut icon, apple-touch-icon and mask-icon on the page with its size and type, the web app manifest link, and whether /favicon.ico exists, all as absolute URLs, with the best icon picked (SVG, then the largest size; mask icons never). Use to show a site's logo next to a link, build bookmarks or enrich a company record. Example: url=https://github.com/. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Page or site URL

tools.name: pack_seo_toolkit
tools.description: One call for an on-page SEO analysis of a URL: the SEO audit (title and description lengths, canonical, headings, alt text, structured data, score, issues), the top keywords and two-word phrases with their density, the social preview (OpenGraph, Twitter card), the favicon, and robots.txt access with its sitemaps. Server HTML only. Cheaper than the tools one by one. Use before publishing, for an SEO report or to compare a competitor's page. Example: url=https://www.wikipedia.org/. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the page

tools.name: tech_stack
tools.description: Detect the technologies behind a website from its home page HTML and response headers: CMS or site builder (WordPress, Shopify, Webflow…), JavaScript framework (Next.js, Nuxt, React…), analytics and ad pixels, support widgets, payments, captcha, CDN and hosting, web server and backend language, each with the evidence that matched. About 90 public fingerprints, server HTML only. Use for lead research, competitor analysis or sales prospecting. Example: url=https://vercel.com/. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Website or page URL

tools.name: extract
tools.description: Fetch any public web page URL and get clean, LLM-ready text or Markdown: main content, code blocks, tables, links and headings, for RAG and agent context. Static HTML, Markdown or text; optional section ID. Default 20,000 output characters, max 100,000; input 2 MiB. No JavaScript rendering (see /extract/rendered), logins or paywalls. Empty pages, bad sections, browser challenges and errors are not charged. Use to read docs or articles. Example: url=https://example.com. Price $0.002/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the page to fetch

maxChars.description: Maximum characters of body text to return (500-100000, default 20000)

format.description: Returned representation: text (default), markdown, or both. HTML structured details are included in every format; Markdown/plain sources have empty details.

section.description: Optional visible HTML ID within primary content, 1-500 characters. A leading # (the fragment a docs link shows) or a URL ending in #id is accepted, and so is a heading's visible text when exactly one heading matches (answered with warning section_matched_by_heading). Heading scope includes subsections until next same/higher-level heading; section/article/main/div scope is its subtree. Missing/ambiguous/unsupported targets fail uncharged, and a miss lists the ids the page does offer under sections. A fragment added to url still does not select a section. Leave it out to read the whole page.

tools.name: extract_rendered
tools.description: Same output as /extract, but the page is first rendered in a real browser, so single-page apps and pages that build their content with JavaScript come back with their text instead of an empty shell. Waits for the network to settle (up to 15 seconds). Public pages only; no login. Use when /extract returns EXTRACTION_EMPTY or too little text for a page you can read in a browser. Example: url=https://example.com/. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits); failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute public http(s) URL of the page

section.description: Optional HTML id to read only that element; a leading #, a URL ending in #id or a unique heading's visible text is accepted

tools.name: pdf_text
tools.description: Extract the text of a public PDF (up to 10 MB) from its URL, page by page, with title, author and page count. Choose the first page, how many pages (up to 200) and maxChars. arXiv abstract links work. If a site blocks our fetch, the Internet Archive's dated copy is read and the answer says so. Scanned, encrypted and non-PDF files fail uncharged. Use to read papers, invoices, reports and manuals into an agent. Example: url=https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf. Price $0.005/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute public http(s) URL of the PDF. With no input at all this reads the published sample (the Bitcoin white paper); send url for your own PDF.

pages.description: How many pages to read (1-200, default 20)

maxChars.description: Maximum characters of text returned across all pages (1000-200000, default 50000)

tools.name: sitemap
tools.description: Sitemap parser: reads one public XML sitemap or sitemap index as structured URLs and source-reported dates. Supports gzip, substring filtering and pagination. Large sitemaps are read from the start (512 KiB, 1000 entries at most, with a warning). Does not crawl pages or follow child sitemaps. Invalid XML and execution errors are not charged; a valid empty match is charged. Use to find which pages of a docs site to read before calling /extract. Example: url=https://www.sitemaps.org/sitemap.xml. Price $0.002/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute public HTTP(S) XML sitemap URL; child sitemaps are not fetched automatically

contains.description: Optional case-insensitive URL substring, at most 200 characters

maxUrls.description: Reported matching locations examined in one page (1-100, default 25); invalid/nonpublic locations may reduce returned entries

offset.description: Offset into distinct reported matching locations (0-1000, default 0); use nextOffset to continue

tools.name: summarize
tools.description: Give a URL, get a short summary of the page plus three to six key points, ready to drop into an agent's context. Fetches the page, strips navigation and boilerplate, and summarizes the main text with an LLM. HTML pages only; for a PDF use pdf_text, then ai_summarize_text. Use for research, news triage, link previews and deciding whether a page is worth reading in full. For the full text use extract. Example: url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTTP_402. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits); failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the page to summarize

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Render any public web page in a real headless Chrome browser, with JavaScript executed, and get a JPEG screenshot (1280 px wide, base64) plus the final URL, HTTP status and page title. Set fullPage=true to capture up to 4000 px of page height. Use for visual checks, page previews, monitoring and feeding pages to vision models. Example: url=https://example.com. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits); failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the page to capture

fullPage.description: Set to true to capture the full page height (max 4000 px) instead of the 1280x800 viewport

tools.name: papers
tools.description: Research papers search across journals, conferences, preprints and books (Crossref): title, authors, year, venue, citation count, DOI link and abstract where available. Optional fromYear filter and up to 20 results per call. Use for research agents, literature reviews, fact-checking a claim against published work, and finding the DOI for a citation. Example: query=CRISPR off-target effects. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits); failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

query.description: Search terms, a title or a research question (3-300 characters)

fromYear.description: Only works published in or after this year

tools.name: arxiv_search
tools.description: Search arXiv, the open preprint server for physics, mathematics, computer science and AI: give search words (every word must match, quotes for a phrase) and optionally a category such as cs.AI, and get 1-20 papers by relevance or newest first, each with title, abstract, authors, dates, categories, DOI and PDF link. An arXiv ID or link returns that paper. Use to find research on a topic, cite a paper or read its abstract before the PDF. Example: q=retrieval augmented generation. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

q.description: Search words, or an arXiv ID or link (1706.03762, arxiv.org/abs/2401.01234)

category.description: Optional arXiv category to search in, e.g. cs.AI, cs.CL, stat.ML, hep-th

tools.name: document_text
tools.description: Convert a document to text or Markdown: Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx), PowerPoint (.pptx), PDF, plain UTF-8 text (.txt/.md/.csv/.json), and scans or images (PNG, JPEG, WebP) by OCR. Give a public URL or POST the file (10 MB default; 10-20 MB URLs retry once at 20 MB; images 3 MB). Old formats and protected files fail uncharged. Use for attachments, scans and spreadsheets in an agent, RAG or workflow. Example: url=https://calibre-ebook.com/downloads/demos/demo.docx. Price $0.005/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits); failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute public http(s) URL of the file (or send the file in a POST body instead)

format.description: markdown (default: headings, lists and tables kept) or text

maxChars.description: Maximum characters of text returned (1000-200000, default 50000)

maxBytes.description: Maximum file size in MB for a URL read (10 default, up to 20). If omitted, a file over 10 MB is retried once at 20 MB; an explicit value is respected

tools.name: document_extract
tools.description: Extract named fields from a document as JSON: give a PDF, Word, Excel or PowerPoint file, a scan or a photo (PNG, JPEG, WebP) by URL or in a POST body (up to 10 MB; images 3 MB) and the field names you want, such as invoice_number, total, due_date. An AI model reads the file, scans by OCR, and returns one JSON object, with null where a value is not stated. Use to turn invoices, receipts, orders and contracts into rows. Price $0.03/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits); failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute public http(s) URL of the file (or send the file in a POST body instead). With no input at all (no URL) this reads the public sample invoice PDF in the example and the answer says so.

fields.description: Comma-separated field names to extract (1-30). For rows, give the row keys in brackets: line_items[description,quantity,amount]. Or one word, invoice or receipt, for the usual fields of that document with its line items

tools.name: feed
tools.description: Read a public RSS 2.0, RSS 1.0 or Atom feed and get the feed title, link and description plus its newest items: title, link, date (ISO 8601), short plain-text summary, author and id. Up to 50 items, feeds up to 2 MB. Lenient with real-world feeds; a page that is not a feed returns 422, uncharged. Use to follow news, blogs, release notes or podcasts without scraping pages. Example: url=https://hnrss.org/frontpage. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute public http(s) URL of the feed, or of a web page whose head links to its feed

tools.name: url_meta
tools.description: Fetch a public web page's head and return link-preview metadata: title, description, site name, type, preview image, canonical URL, language, author, published time, favicon, theme colour, and every OpenGraph and Twitter-card field. Reads at most 1 MB and never runs JavaScript. Use to build link previews, label citations or check how a URL will unfurl before sharing it. Example: url=https://github.com/. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute public http(s) URL of the page

tools.name: agent_readiness
tools.description: Score how ready a website is for AI agents, 0-100: llms.txt, sitemap, OpenAPI spec, MCP server card, A2A agent card and x402 payment discovery, each found or missing with its URL, which AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and others) robots.txt lets in, and a list of fixes. Reads only the public files a site publishes; nothing is signed in or submitted. Use to audit your own site or vet a service before an agent relies on it. Example: url=https://stripe.com. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: The site: a domain or any URL on it (its origin is checked)

tools.name: robots
tools.description: Read a site's robots.txt and say whether a crawler may fetch a URL, by RFC 9309 rules as Google applies them (most specific user-agent group, longest matching Allow or Disallow, Allow on ties, * and $ wildcards). Returns the deciding rule, the group used, the rule count and the sitemaps listed. A missing robots.txt (4xx) allows everything. Use before scraping or crawling a site politely; for the sitemap URLs themselves use sitemap. Example: url=https://www.google.com/search. Price $0.001/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: The page URL to check (its site's /robots.txt is read)

agent.description: Crawler user agent or product token (default *)

tools.name: url_redirects
tools.description: Follow a URL's redirects hop by hop (up to 10) and return every hop's status code and Location, the final URL, total hops, timing and whether it loops. Expands short links (bit.ly, t.co…) to their destination without loading the page. Every hop is checked before it is requested; redirects to private addresses are reported, not followed. Use to unshorten a link, check an HTTPS or www redirect, or debug SEO redirect chains. Example: url=http://github.com. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL

tools.name: url_uptime
tools.description: Check whether a website is up right now: one live request (following redirects) with the HTTP status, up or down, response time in ms, the final URL, content type, server header and page size, and optionally whether the page contains a given text. Timeouts and connection failures come back as down with the reason, not as an error. Use for uptime monitoring, health checks before calling an API, or to confirm a deploy. Example: url=https://www.wikipedia.org/. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL

contains.description: Optional text that must appear in the page (first 500 KB)

tools.name: seo_audit
tools.description: On-page SEO audit of one URL: title and meta description with their lengths, canonical, meta robots, H1s and H2 count, images without alt text, lang and viewport, Open Graph and Twitter card tags, JSON-LD blocks, internal and external link counts and word count, plus a list of issues and a 0-100 score. Reads the server's HTML (no JavaScript), up to 1 MB. Use to check a page before publishing or to compare competitors. Example: url=https://www.wikipedia.org/. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the page

tools.name: audit_website
tools.description: WCAG 2.1 A/AA accessibility violations with axe-core (rule, impact, elements, fix link) on one URL from a single load in a real browser, plus page speed (first byte, FCP, LCP, layout shift) and page weight by type, on-page SEO on the rendered page, and HTTP security headers with a grade. One overall score and the top issues. Use for a site or client report, before a launch, or to compare competitors. Example: url=https://www.wikipedia.org/. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits); failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the page to audit

tools.name: page_publish
tools.description: Publish an HTML page and get a public URL for it (valid up to 7 days): send the HTML (up to 200,000 characters) and an optional title; the page is sanitised (no scripts, styles, frames, forms or event handlers; links and https images stay), screened by content moderation, stored, and served at /p/<id> with noindex. Use to hand a person a report, table or summary your agent produced, or to share results between agents. Removal requests: /support. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits); failed calls free. Publishes a page on the public web that stays up until it expires and cannot be withdrawn; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

html.description: The HTML to publish (body content or a full document), up to 200,000 characters

title.description: Page title (default: the first line of text)

days.description: Days the page stays online, 1 to 7 (default 7)

tools.name: wikipedia
tools.description: Short summary of a Wikipedia article in any language edition: title, one-paragraph extract, description, thumbnail and page URL. Use to ground an agent's answer in a quick, citable fact sheet. Example: title=Stockholm. Price $0.002/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.

tools.name: dictionary
tools.description: Dictionary definition of an English word from Wiktionary, grouped by part of speech, with example sentences where Wiktionary gives them, plus the page link and the CC BY-SA attribution to show. Use for writing help, vocabulary, translation checks and word games. Example: word=serendipity. Price $0.01/call via x402 USDC or a card key (/credits), first 10 free; failed calls free. Reads or computes only and changes nothing; each call is charged, so repeats are not free.
